messages.author: 628053524651bedc
messages.subject: probe2WayMC() - valProbe?
parts:
ould somebody please clarify the valProbe argument for me?
I seem to have blockade in my understanding.

I have reviewed the document file:
" The values of the moderator that will be used to probe the effect of the focal predictor."

My moderator was measured by three items on a scale from -3 to +3.
The summary of the standardized latent factor scores reads as follows:

Min. :-1.3184
1st Qu.:-0.8861
Median :-0.1293
Mean : 0.0000
3rd Qu.: 0.7842
Max. : 1.7996

After experimenting with probe values, I see the two "probed" regressions rotating which makes perfectly sense to me. In conclusion, I was wondering
a) what are the appropriate values to probe for and
b) can I create a graph that represents how the lines behave for meaningful different probes?

My confusion/question probably arose after reading:
https://www.deadreckoning.consulting/blog/2018/07/11/2018-07-12-interaction-plots-with-continuous-moderators-in-r/


Any comment is much appreciated.

Carsten

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: probe2WayMC() - valProbe?
parts: My moderator was measured by three items on a scale from -3 to +3.

probe2WayMC() is only for latent interactions.   The relevant scale is the moderating factor's SD (square-root of fixed/estimated total variance).  If it is an endogenous factor, you could obtain this from lavInspect(fit, "cov.lv") and lavInspect(fit, "mean.lv")
a) what are the appropriate values to probe for
A good default is the M along with 1 SD above and below M.
b) can I create a graph that represents how the lines behave for meaningful different probes?

My confusion/question probably arose after reading:
https://www.deadreckoning.consulting/blog/2018/07/11/2018-07-12-interaction-plots-with-continuous-moderators-in-r/

Yes, that would be confusing.  That blog post does not inspire me to recommend hiring that consultant.  He does not even fit a latent interaction, but a bifactor model.  He loads all first-order (not product) indicators on a general factor he confuses with a latent interaction.  I recommend using our help-page examples for guidance instead.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: probe2WayMC() - valProbe?
parts:
I'm pretty skeptical of how useful a J-N region of significance is for latent interactions. The point of a J-N region of significance is to identify values of the moderator where the simple slope is different from 0. This is useful if specific values of the moderator have a meaningful interpretation. But with a latent moderator, the scale of the moderator is arbitrary (since we're setting the scale) so the specific values of the moderator where a simple slope differs from 0 isn't very helpful. 

With a latent moderator we're usually interested in how the slope of the focal predictor changes across values of the moderator, which simple slopes can help with. A plot of simple slopes and values of the moderator (like is often presented with H-N intervals) could be useful. It's not available in plotProbe right now, but it's something we can put on the to do list. For now if you want to generate a plot like that the best option might be a web calculator that will give you R code for a plot like that (like the one at: http://quantpsy.org/interact/mlr2.htm).
